gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured idle (no-load) draw for any 12V inverter: DD Solar measured a 12V 2000W pure-sine component inverter at 11.6 W idle (about 280 Wh a day) and 85.5–87.3% efficient, and a Victron owner bench-measured the Phoenix 12/1200 at 10.0 W at 12 V against Victron's 7 W spec. No named reviewer has published a measurement for ACOPOWER, ALLWEI or PowMr's 12V all-in-ones.
standout_why: ChatGPT's 12 results are all renogy.com pages: three kit pages, the REGO 12V 3000W inverter charger, the 2000W/3000W HF inverter charger, the split-phase blog and the RV Solution page. None is marked as cited. I could not open the two Renogy inverter pages (renogy.com returned HTTP 429 to both WebFetch and storecheck), so I judged them only by their titles and by ChatGPT's answer. Neither those titles nor the answer give any idle-draw or efficiency figure, measured or spec, for any unit. The answer recommends ACOPOWER, ALLWEI and PowMr with prices only. The measured figures I found are new, but they come from 12V component inverters, not from the three all-in-ones ChatGPT recommended. So they help with a framing question (all-in-one vs separate MPPT plus inverter), not with ranking the candidates. That is why the score is 1 rather than 2.
decides: This doesn't pick between ACOPOWER, ALLWEI and PowMr, because none has a named measurement. It does give the page a sourced baseline: a 12V component inverter measured at 10–11.6 W idle, which is 240–280 Wh a day from a 12V battery. The page can tell shoppers to check a 12V all-in-one's listed no-load draw against that figure before choosing an all-in-one over a separate MPPT plus inverter. That matters most in vans and RVs with a single 100Ah (1.28 kWh) battery. Any all-in-one idle figures have to be labelled as maker specs.

findings.product: Datouboss SAK 2000W 12V pure sine inverter (sold as MFUZOP; PCB S-PSW-12V-110V-2000W)
findings.label: Measured idle (no-load) draw
findings.source_title: Budget Friendly! 12V 2000W Sine Inverter: Full Test, Analysis, Teardown Insights (solarpoweredge.com)
findings.note: Measured by Dave (DD Solar, blog user ddsolar2020). Published 2026-02-19, with long-term updates to 2026-04-15. Inverter powered on with no load. This is a component inverter with no built-in MPPT; the test rig charged its batteries through a separate 60 A MakeSkyBlue MPPT. 11.6 W × 24 h = 278 Wh.

findings.label: Measured DC-to-AC efficiency
findings.value: 85.5% at 168.8 W out (about 8% load); 87.3% at 1,028 W out (about 51% load)
findings.source_title: Budget Friendly! 12V 2000W Sine Inverter: Full Test, Analysis, Teardown Insights (solarpoweredge.com)
findings.note: Measured by DD Solar, 2026-02-19. 168.8 W AC out from 197.36 W DC in = 85.5%. 1,028 W AC out from 1,177.4 W DC in = 87.3%. DC input current was 91.2 A at about 1 kW. AC output was about 111 V.

findings.label: Bench-measured zero-load power vs datasheet
findings.value: 10.0 W at 12 V input and 12.9 W at 14 V, against a 7 W datasheet figure
findings.source_title: Phoenix 1200/12 – Zero-load power much higher than specified (measured 10 W vs. 7 W), Victron Community
findings.note: Measured by forum user Ståle (staldor), post dated 2025-10-16. New unit, no load, fan off, about 20 °C. Input set and measured with a lab power supply and checked with a multimeter; instrument models and calibration not given. Full series: 10 V 7.4 W, 11 V 8.5 W, 12 V 10.0 W, 13 V 11.3 W, 14 V 12.9 W. Idle draw rises with battery voltage, so a charged LiFePO4 at about 13.3 V idles above the datasheet figure.
